\documentclass{beamer}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\title{Derivatives}
\begin{document}
\begin{frame}{Rules}
  \begin{itemize}[<+->]
    \item Power rule: $\frac{d}{dx} x^n = n x^{n-1}$
    \item Product rule: $(fg)' = f'g + fg'$
    \item Chain rule: $(f\circ g)' = (f'\circ g)\, g'$
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Steps}
  First $x^2$.\pause\ Then $x^3$.\pause\ Finally $x^4$.
  \onslide<2->{This appears from step 2.}
  \visible<3>{Only visible on step 3.}
  \alt<1>{Early}{Late}
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}[fragile]{Code}
\begin{verbatim}
def f(x):
    return x**2
\end{verbatim}
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Limits}
  \[ \lim_{h\to 0} \frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} \]
  \pause
  is the derivative at $x$.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
